newsitem.title: UK: DBS Management gains as profits rise 84 pct.
newsitem.headline: DBS Management gains as profits rise 84 pct.

text.p: Shares in financial services group DBS Management Plc rose on Wednesday after the company posted nearly-doubled profits for the past year and said the current year had started well.
The stock was up 37-1/2p at 10.17-1/2 stg by 1220 GMT in volume of 66,091 shares -- continuing a steady advance which has seen the price more than double since it ended 1996 at 488p.

DBS, which runs the UK's biggest network of independent financial advisers, played down the potential impact of a current review of the selling of pension products by the Personal Investment Authority, an industry regulator.
It said 420,000 stg had been set aside to cover the costs of the review but no other provision was being taken against any such potential liabilities.
DBS reported an 84-percent rise in pre-tax profit to 6.2 million stg, after costs of more than half a million stg related to its elevation to a full listing on the London Stock Exchange.
Turnover rose 45 percent to 111.5 million stg and the full-year dividend was raised to 18p per share from 12p.
"The board believes that the steady trend towards independent advice, which has now prevailed since 1993, will continue," DBS said.

"These twin factors represent a significant opportunity to the group, and the board looks forward to continuing progress during the new financial year. This trend has been borne out by an encouraging start to trading in the new financial year."
